cultural.vision_reason: A finely carved wooden figure of a seated woman with cedar-bark skirt, plaited hair, and childhood head-flattening — all features consistent with Northwest Coast (Kwakwaka'wakw) carving traditions and material culture.

physical.title: figure
physical.summary: Carved wood figure of a woman sitting on her haunches, with her legs sharply drawn up, the feet facing in, touching toe to toe in front of her cedar bark skirt (depicted with incised lines for a belt, with vertical lines for the hanging bark). The torso is left schematic, the face is realistically carved with raised lips and nose, circular eyes in lozenge shaped excavated areas. The head indicates childhood flattening, with a central parting and three strand plaits on either side, one held in each hand. This is finely carved, and originally featured a fine surface of small knife or chisel cuts, such as might have been made with beaver teeth or a small metal curved knife. It is however very much worn, with most of the surface rubbed away, except on the legs and back.
